label: late absolute time step in the copy phase (t >= 14)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of activation mass), at late absolute time steps of the sequence, so effectively only in long sequences (L=8,9 carry 99% of mass). Firing rate rises sharply with t: ~0 before t=12, 4% at t=12, 22% at t=13, 66% at t=14, 88% at t=15, ~96% at t=16-17; mass share is concentrated at t>=14. Activation within a sequence typically ramps up over successive copy steps and peaks at the final 1-2 outputs (top examples peak at the last step of L=9 sequences). Largely independent of token identity (input/output token lifts are flat ~1-2x); mild increase with repeated tokens/more digits. Does not fire in the original phase, on the delimiter, or anywhere in short sequences (L<=6). Misses are weak onsets at t=13; false positives are mostly t=14-15 steps in L=8 sequences where activation has not yet built up.

issues: The main claims hold. Test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.836, R 0.856, F1 0.846, mass recall 0.955). The copy phase holds 100% of the activation mass and L=8 plus L=9 hold 98.7% of it. The firing rates by t match the stated figures (t=12 0.044, t=13 0.218, t=14 0.662, t=15 0.882, t=16-17 about 0.96). Token lifts are flat.

One side claim is a confound and should be dropped: 'activation rises slightly when tokens repeat or the sequence has more digits'. Within a fixed (L,t) cell neither has any effect. L=8,t=14: n_digits==0 gives precision 0.575, in_count>=2 gives 0.556, against a cell average of 0.56. L=9,t=14: n_digits==0 gives 0.766, n_digits>=3 gives 0.752; in_count==1 gives 0.763, in_count>=2 gives 0.766. L=9,t=13: n_digits==0 gives 0.155, n_digits>=3 gives 0.13. The marginal lifts appear only because longer sequences (and so later t) contain more digits and repeats.

The effect of t is not purely absolute, because sequence length interacts with it non-monotonically. Firing rate on test: at t=12, L=7 0.055, L=8 0.073, L=9 0.003; at t=13, L=7 0.165, L=8 0.34, L=9 0.151; at t=14, L=8 0.56, L=9 0.763. So shorter sequences start firing earlier (at their last outputs) but saturate lower. This is a graded onset, not a separate class of counterexamples.

On the test split the false positives are not only L=8,t=14: L=9,t=14 also sits at 76% precision. Misses include the last copy steps of L=7 sequences at t=13 (16.5% rate). All of these are weak activations at onset. Predicates that exclude L=8,t=14 or condition on n_digits lowered F1 (0.821).
